title: Engine cranks slowly
h1: Why does my engine crank slowly?
metaDesc: Engine turning over slowly when you start it? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's the battery, cables or starter, and how soon to deal with it.
synonyms: turns over slow in the morning
intro: A slow crank is often the first warning before a car won't start at all. Usually the battery is weak or a connection is poor, but a tired starter or a problem inside the engine can sound similar. Answer the questions below to find the likely cause and how soon to act.
safety: If you smell burning or see smoke near the battery, cables or starter, stop trying to start it.
If the battery is swollen, cracked or leaking, don't jump or charge it.
Don't crank for more than 10 seconds at a time. Wait about a minute between tries so the starter doesn't overheat.

q_what_happens.q: What happens when you try to start it?
q_what_happens.help: Cranking is the rrr-rrr-rrr sound of the engine turning over before it fires. A slow crank sounds drawn out and labored, like rrrr... rrrr... rrrr.

opts.a: It cranks slowly but does start
It cranks slowly, then gives up or turns into clicking
I smell burning or see smoke near the engine or battery
The engine turns a little, then stops hard with a thunk, or this started after driving through deep water

q_when.q: When is the slow crank worst?

opts.a: When the engine is hot, right after a drive
After the car has sat for a few days
Every time, and it's slowly getting worse

q_jump.q: Does a jump start or battery booster make it crank at normal speed?

opts.a: Yes, it cranks quickly and starts
No, it's still slow even with a good jump

result.title: A cable, connection or the starter may be overheating
result.now: Stop trying to start it and step away from the car. Once nothing is smoking, have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If smoke keeps coming or you see flames, get everyone away from the car and call 911.
If the smell was only faint and faded right away, still don't keep cranking. A shorted cable can start a fire.
result.why: A burning smell while cranking usually means a lot of current is going somewhere it shouldn't, or the starter is straining against something. Heavy battery and starter cables carry enough power to melt insulation.

causes.name: Starter motor overheating or shorted
causes.clues: Smell or smoke from low on the engine, after long or repeated cranking.

causes.name: Damaged or shorted battery cable
causes.clues: Melted or chafed insulation, or a cable that's hot to the touch.

causes.name: Engine not turning freely
causes.clues: The crank was labored or stopped abruptly.

shop: Battery cable and starter wiring inspection
Check that the engine turns freely by hand

result.title: Something may be stopping the engine from turning
result.now: Don't keep trying to start it. Have it towed to a shop.
if: If this happened after driving through deep water, water may be in the engine. Cranking it again can bend internal parts.
result.why: A healthy engine spins evenly when cranking, even if slowly. If it stops hard with a thunk, something inside may be blocking it, such as water or coolant in a cylinder, or a seized part. Forcing it with the starter can turn a fixable problem into a major one.

causes.name: Water or coolant in a cylinder
causes.clues: Recent deep water, white smoke before, or coolant level dropping.

causes.name: Seized or damaged engine part
causes.clues: Knocking, an oil light or low oil before this started.

causes.name: Starter gear jamming
causes.clues: A grinding sound, and the engine seemed fine before.

you: Check the oil level on the dipstick without starting the engine.
shop: Turn the engine over by hand
Check cylinders for water or coolant

result.title: The battery may be getting weak, and cold makes it show
result.now: Have the battery tested soon. Many auto parts stores do this free. A load test shows whether it needs replacing, which is more likely if it's more than 4 years old.
if: If the battery tests good, ask for a charging test and check the battery cables for corrosion.
If the slow crank turns into clicking, it's close to leaving you stranded. Have the battery charged and tested right away.
If you smell burning or see smoke near the battery, cables or starter, stop trying to start it.
result.why: Cold weather lowers how much power a battery can deliver and makes engine oil thicker, so the starter has to work harder. A battery that's starting to fail often shows it first on cold mornings.

causes.name: Aging battery
causes.clues: It's more than 4 years old, and it's fine once the day warms up.

causes.name: Corroded or loose battery cables
causes.clues: Buildup on the terminals.

causes.name: Oil that's too thick for the season
causes.clues: A recent oil change with a different oil than your owner's manual lists.

you: Check the date on the battery.
Look at the terminals for buildup.
Check your owner's manual for the right oil.
shop: Voltage-drop test on the battery cables

result.title: The starter may be wearing out, especially when hot
result.now: Have the battery and starter tested at your next opportunity. A shop can measure how much power the starter draws.
if: If it sometimes won't crank at all when hot, but starts after it cools, the starter or its wiring may be close to failing. Get it checked soon.
If it's also slow when cold, start with the battery and cables.
If you smell burning while cranking, stop trying to start it.
result.why: Heat from the engine raises the electrical resistance in a worn starter and its cables. A starter that's on its way out often cranks slowly or not at all when hot, then works again once things cool down. A shop will usually test the cables and ground connections before replacing the starter.

causes.name: Worn starter motor
causes.clues: Slow or no crank only when the engine is hot.

causes.name: Poor cable connection at the starter or ground
causes.clues: It comes and goes, and the battery tests fine.

causes.name: Weak battery
causes.clues: It's also slow on cold mornings.
causes.against: If it's only slow when hot, the battery is less likely.

you: Note whether it only happens after a drive.
shop: Voltage-drop test on starter cables and ground

result.title: The battery may be draining while the car sits
result.now: Have the battery tested. If it's healthy, watch whether the slow crank only happens after the car sits.
if: If it only happens after a week or more of sitting, a battery maintainer may be all you need.
If it happens after just a night or two, ask a shop for a parasitic draw test.
If the battery is swollen, cracked or leaking, don't jump or charge it. Have it replaced by a shop.
result.why: Cars use a little power even when off. If something stays on, or the battery is aging, a few days of sitting leaves too little charge to spin the starter at full speed.

causes.name: Something staying on while parked
causes.clues: A trunk, glove box or dome light that stays on, or an added accessory.

causes.name: Aging battery
causes.clues: It's more than 4 years old.

causes.name: Short trips not recharging the battery
causes.clues: Mostly drives of a few minutes.

you: Check for lights that stay on after you lock the car.
Check the date on the battery.

result.title: Often a weak battery or a poor battery connection
result.now: Check that the battery clamps are clean and tight, then have the battery and charging system tested. Many auto parts stores do this free.
if: If the battery and cables test fine, the starter is the next thing to test. A shop will usually do a voltage-drop test on the cables before replacing the starter.
If the battery light has come on while driving, have the alternator tested too.
If you smell burning or see smoke while cranking, stop trying to start it.
If the engine was knocking, or the oil light was on before this started, don't keep cranking. Have it checked.
result.why: The starter needs a big burst of power. A weak battery or a corroded connection can't deliver it, so the engine turns slowly. These are common causes and the easiest to check.

causes.name: Weak or aging battery
causes.clues: It's more than 4 years old, or it's worse on cold mornings.

causes.name: Corroded or loose battery cable or ground
causes.clues: Buildup on the terminals, or a clamp that moves by hand.

causes.name: Worn starter
causes.clues: The battery tests good but the crank is still slow.

you: Check the date on the battery.
Try a jump start and see if it cranks faster.
shop: Voltage-drop test on the battery cables

result.title: The battery may be low. Find out why before it leaves you stranded
result.now: If it started on a jump, a longer drive helps put some charge back, but it won't fully recharge a flat battery. Get the battery and charging system tested within the next few days.
if: If the battery light comes on while driving, the alternator may not be charging and the car could stall once the battery runs down. Get it to a shop as soon as possible, and avoid long trips and night driving.
If the battery is more than 4 years old, a load test will show whether it needs replacing.
result.why: A jump fixing the slow crank suggests the battery didn't have enough charge. The question is whether the battery is worn out, isn't being recharged, or is being drained while parked.

causes.name: Aging battery
causes.clues: More than 4 years old, or slow cranks on cold mornings.

causes.name: Alternator not charging
causes.clues: The battery light flickers or stays on, or the lights dim at idle.

causes.name: Drain while parked
causes.clues: It's worst after the car sits.

you: Watch for the battery warning light.
Check the date on the battery.

result.title: Possibly a failing starter or a bad cable connection
result.now: Check that the battery clamps are clean and tight. If it still cranks slowly with a good jump, book a starter and cable test.
if: If it stops cranking altogether, have it towed or call a mobile mechanic rather than cranking over and over.
If you smell burning while cranking, stop right away.
If the engine was knocking, or the oil light was on before this started, don't keep cranking. The engine itself may be hard to turn.
result.why: When a good jump doesn't speed up the crank, the battery is less likely to be the main problem. Power may be getting lost in a cable or ground connection, or the starter itself may be worn and drawing too much current. A shop will usually test the cables before replacing the starter.

causes.name: Worn starter motor
causes.clues: It's worse when hot, or it has been getting slower over months.

causes.name: Corroded cable or engine ground strap
causes.clues: A cable that's warm after cranking, or corrosion at either end.

causes.name: Engine harder to turn than normal
causes.clues: Wrong oil, or a recent engine problem.

you: Clean and tighten the battery clamps.
Look for a loose or broken ground strap between the engine and body.
shop: Voltage-drop test on the positive cable and ground
